title: Use-time checkpoint binding and consume/checkpoint reconciliation
supported_claim: On the tested same-host SQLite prototype, a platform-issued use-time integrity token bound to the exact current checkpoint, pre-consumption canonical ledger state, convergence permit binding, authority epoch, and one-time token identity prevented stale checkpoint reuse after the tested intervening ledger mutations. Permit consumption and creation of a durable PENDING reconciliation record occurred in one SQLite transaction; PENDING survived restart, could not be silently settled by restart, an old or same-generation checkpoint, or a wrong-digest higher-generation checkpoint, and was settled exactly once by an authenticated strictly higher-generation checkpoint over the exact recorded post-consumption ledger state. Concurrent same-token consumers produced at most one terminal convergence transition. Reviewer/model inputs gained no production or release authority.
not_proven: Atomic commitment between SQLite and a truly external checkpoint service
Protection after compromise of all local permit, integrity, and token keys
Tamper resistance or independent integrity of the convergence_reconciliation table itself
Global uniqueness of unconsumed use-time token nonces at issuance
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 6: reconciliation-ledger integrity. Protect PENDING/SETTLED reconciliation records against coherent local rewrite, deletion, rollback, post-digest substitution, checkpoint-generation lowering, and forged settlement state without widening convergence or release authority.
